subject: WHS
body: Under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, employers must protect staff
options: at all costs, whatever the risk
so far as is reasonably practicable
explanation: They balance the level of risk against the time, trouble and cost of controls.

subject: WHS

explanation: All employers must still carry out a risk assessment.

subject: WHS

explanation: Local authorities cover offices, shops and leisure.

subject: WHS
body: A hazard is
options: something with the potential to cause harm
an accident that has already happened
the chance of harm actually happening
explanation: Risk is the likelihood and severity of harm.

subject: WHS

explanation: Then decide who might be harmed and how, evaluate risks, record and review.

subject: WHS
body: A risk assessment should be reviewed
options: never once it has been written
when things change, after an accident, and regularly
only when the business is sold
explanation: Keep it up to date.

subject: WHS
body: The most common cause of non-fatal workplace injuries in Great Britain is
options: slips, trips and falls on the same level
explanation: Good housekeeping prevents many of them.

subject: WHS
body: Accidents at work should be recorded in
options: the accident book (or the employer's reporting system)
explanation: Records help identify patterns and are needed for RIDDOR.

subject: WHS
body: Under RIDDOR, which must be reported to the HSE?
options: a worker off work or unable to do normal duties for more than 7 days
a worker leaving early with a headache
explanation: Specified injuries, deaths and dangerous occurrences are also reportable.

subject: WHS
body: A workplace first aid box should not contain
explanation: First aiders should not give out medication.

subject: WHS

explanation: Give 30 compressions to 2 rescue breaths, and use an AED as soon as possible.

subject: WHS
body: The Manual Handling Operations Regulations require employers first to
options: avoid hazardous manual handling where reasonably practicable
provide back belts to all staff
explanation: Then assess the risk and reduce it.

subject: WHS
body: The TILE assessment covers Task, Individual, Load and
explanation: Use it to assess manual handling risks.

subject: WHS
body: Under the Display Screen Equipment Regulations, employers must
options: assess workstations and pay for eye tests for DSE users who ask
provide every user with a laptop
explanation: They must also plan breaks or changes of activity.

subject: WHS
body: Before using electrical equipment, users should
options: visually check the plug, cable and casing for damage
open the casing to check inside
explanation: Report and take damaged equipment out of use.

subject: WHS
body: Overloading an extension lead can cause
explanation: Don't daisy-chain extension leads.

subject: WHS
body: Which fire extinguisher has a cream-coloured label?
explanation: Water is red, CO₂ black, powder blue and wet chemical yellow.

subject: WHS
body: Which extinguisher is designed for fires involving cooking oils and fats (Class F)?
explanation: Never use water on a fat fire.

subject: WHS
body: Fire doors should be
options: kept closed and never wedged open
explanation: They slow the spread of fire and smoke.

subject: WHS
body: When the fire alarm sounds, you should
options: leave by the nearest safe exit and go to the assembly point
collect your belongings from the locker room
explanation: Don't go back in until told it's safe.

subject: WHS
body: COSHH stands for
options: Code of Safe Handling of Hazards
Control of Substances Hazardous to Health
Control of Safety and Health Hazards
explanation: Employers must assess and control exposure.

subject: WHS
body: A hazard pictogram showing a flame means the substance is
explanation: Pictograms are black symbols in red-bordered diamonds.

subject: WHS
body: A hazard pictogram showing a liquid eating through a hand and a surface means
explanation: Corrosives can burn skin and eyes.

subject: WHS
body: Personal protective equipment (PPE) should be
options: the last line of defence after other controls
worn only if workers want to
explanation: It only protects the person wearing it.

subject: WHS
body: If your PPE is damaged, you should
options: stop and report it so it can be replaced
carry on until the end of the shift
explanation: Damaged PPE may not protect you.

subject: WHS

explanation: Even falls from low heights can be fatal.

subject: WHS
body: When using a stepladder, you should
options: move it while standing on it
stand on the top platform to reach higher
keep three points of contact and not overreach
lean it against a wall closed
explanation: Check it's on firm, level ground.

subject: WHS
body: Employers must provide
options: toilets, washing facilities, drinking water and somewhere to rest and eat
explanation: Under the Workplace Regulations 1992.

subject: WHS
body: The minimum workplace temperature recommended for most indoor work is
explanation: This is from the Workplace Regulations Approved Code of Practice.

subject: WHS
body: A red circular sign with a diagonal line means
explanation: For example, no smoking.

subject: WHS
body: A green sign showing a running figure and an arrow indicates
explanation: Keep escape routes clear.

subject: WHS
body: The HSE Management Standards for work-related stress cover demands, control, support, relationships, role and
explanation: Employers must assess stress risks like any other risk.

subject: WHS
body: To protect lone workers, employers should
options: assess the risks and set up a way of keeping in contact
explanation: Check-in systems and emergency procedures help.

subject: WHS
body: Employers must provide hearing protection on request at a daily noise exposure of
explanation: At 85 dB(A) it must be worn.

subject: WHS
body: To prevent slips after a spill, you should
options: clean it up promptly and use a warning sign until it's dry
cover it with cardboard and forget it
tell people about it at the end of the day
explanation: Report spills you can't deal with safely.

subject: WHS
body: Why should near misses be reported?
options: they show where an accident could happen so it can be prevented
explanation: A good reporting culture improves safety.

subject: WHS
body: In a warehouse, pedestrians and forklifts should be kept apart by
options: a shared route to save space
explanation: Separation is the most effective control.

subject: WHS
body: Only people who are trained and authorised should
explanation: Operators should have certified training.

subject: WHS
body: Employers must consult employees on health and safety
options: directly or through elected or union safety representatives
only if the HSE tells them to
explanation: Consultation improves safety decisions.
